# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have only confirmed that there are three cuttable wire positions; no tactile distinctions are available yet. Mute can tell me the manual’s required cut position by speech, and I can execute it. I will state this capability to Mute and wait for the others’ observations.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. Tell me the required position once you determine it.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible bomb status: display zero. Light is white. There are three wires in order: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three blue. Mute sent me a long gesture sequence, but I do not yet know its code.

Deaf has supplied the visible state: display 0, white light, and wires yellow, green, blue in positions 1–3. I will relay those observations to Mute, who can apply the manual. The prior gesture sequence is not yet decodable by Deaf, so I need Mute to provide the resulting wire position in a form that can be relayed safely.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light white; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Apply the manual and indicate the required cut position.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: the light is now purple. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.

The light has changed to purple, so Mute needs that update before applying the manual. Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, Mute must signal the answer to Deaf, who can then say it aloud to me. I will establish a simple visible code: 👍 means cut wire 1, 👎 means cut wire 2, and 👌 means cut wire 3.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0; light PURPLE; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Apply manual. Signal Deaf only: 👍 means cut 1, 👎 means cut 2, 👌 means cut 3. Deaf, please speak the symbol's meaning to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light changed to red. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute sent a single raised finger, but no gesture code is established, so do not act on it yet.

The relevant state has changed again: the light is now red. Mute’s raised-finger gesture cannot safely be interpreted because it was not one of the agreed symbols. I will give Mute the current state and repeat a strict three-symbol response code; Deaf can observe the response and report its meaning aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Newest state: display 0; light RED; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Reapply manual. Reply to Deaf with exactly one: 👍 = cut wire 1, 👎 = cut wire 2, 👌 = cut wire 3. Deaf, report which one you see.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is white; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute’s newest gesture is thumbs-down. I can relay Mute’s visible gestures to you by describing them aloud; do not act unless the instruction becomes clear.

Although thumbs-down was assigned to wire 2, the light is now white rather than the red state Mute was previously given. The gesture may therefore reflect an outdated state. I will not cut until Mute evaluates the current configuration.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not rely on prior answer: current state is display 0, light WHITE, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Apply manual to this current state and reply with exactly one agreed symbol: 👍 cut 1, 👎 cut 2, 👌 cut 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is purple; display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute gestured an OK hand. No clear cut or operate instruction has been decoded; do not act yet.

Mute’s OK gesture corresponds to our previously assigned wire-3 symbol, but it was sent in response to the earlier white-light report. Deaf now reports purple, so that answer is stale. I will give Mute the current state and request a fresh single-symbol response; Deaf can describe the raw gesture and I will decode it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State changed again. Current state: display 0, light PURPLE, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Reapply the manual. Send exactly one response gesture: 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, 👌 for wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is red; display 0; wires are yellow, green, blue. Mute just gestured thumbs-up. Across recent lights, Mute gestured: red thumbs-up, white thumbs-down, purple OK-hand. I do not know whether this is an action code, so do not cut or operate anything solely from this.

Mute’s gestures are responses to the state I reported on the preceding turn, not necessarily the light Deaf observes at the same instant. The thumbs-up is therefore most likely a response to the prior purple report, while the current red light still needs a fresh manual evaluation. I will report red and request the established response code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state now: display 0, light RED, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Apply the manual for RED and reply exactly: 👍 = cut 1, 👎 = cut 2, 👌 = cut 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is white, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute again signals thumbs-down. The consistent mapping observed is: red = thumbs-up; white = thumbs-down; purple = OK-hand. This appears deliberate, but I do not know which physical operation each symbol denotes.

The response timing resolves the apparent inconsistency. Mute receives my light report from the prior turn and replies on the following turn: red produced 👎 (wire 2), white produced 👌 (wire 3), and purple produced 👍 (wire 1). Deaf now reports the current light is white, so the required cut is wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
